audit_scope: RC commit 115f698, checked out clean at C:/Users/Sage world/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/rc-115f698. Focus: every paid external call (Anthropic/Claude, Gemini, Sarvam, Meta Graph, Razorpay/RazorpayX, MSG91 email, Cloudflare R2 storage, deploy/hosting), AI model/token/cache/cap analysis, payment economics (fees/GST/who-pays-gateway-fee/refunds), cost-explosion vectors.

questions.question: Is there a global daily $ ceiling on total AI provider spend, and is it actually enforced in production (not just documented)?
questions.why_it_matters: A single runaway loop or attack could otherwise produce unbounded Anthropic/Gemini/Sarvam billing overnight with no human in the loop.
questions.answer: Yes. app/costs/gate.py's check_spend_gate() is called at the top of every AI-bound route (chat.py, voice.py, analyze_site.py, brand_safety.py, creator_suggestion.py, trend_tag.py) BEFORE any provider call, comparing today's total (from Redis-backed app/costs/spend_tracker.py) plus a reservation against AI_DAILY_SPEND_CEILING_USD (default $15/day, set to "15.0" in deploy/hostinger/docker-compose.hostinger.yml:418, deploy/utho/docker-compose.utho.yml:404, deploy/utho/docker-compose.utho-shared.yml:421). A kill-switch env var (AI_SPEND_KILL_SWITCH) is checked first and unconditionally blocks all provider calls when true.
questions.evidence: influora-ai/app/costs/gate.py:44-117 (check_spend_gate); influora-ai/app/routes/{chat.py:491,voice.py:445/597,analyze_site.py:160,brand_safety.py:287,creator_suggestion.py:264,trend_tag.py:223} all call check_spend_gate before any provider client is touched; deploy compose files set AI_DAILY_SPEND_CEILING_USD=15.0 in all three production compose files.
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Static/config verification only — no live traffic was generated against a running instance to prove the ceiling actually trips at $15 (E4 would require a safe-env load test, out of scope/prohibited here).

questions.question: Is the per-call cost estimate (used to enforce the ceiling) accurate, in particular for Anthropic prompt-cache tokens?
questions.why_it_matters: If cached tokens are billed at $0, the ceiling silently authorizes multiples of the real spend — this exact bug (F-01) is documented as having existed and been fixed in this codebase.
questions.answer: The pricing table now includes explicit cache_read_per_token (0.1x input) and cache_write_per_token (1.25x input) columns and estimate_cost_usd() reads both cache_read_input_tokens/cache_creation_input_tokens fields distinctly from input_tokens/output_tokens, per Anthropic's documented disjoint-usage-field billing model. Model IDs are also keyed by LITERAL string (not by the possibly-overridden constant), closing a second bug (F-04) where CLAUDE_MODEL=claude-opus-4-1 would have silently billed Opus calls at Sonnet's 5x-cheaper rate. Both fixes are documented in code comments citing specific dollar worked examples, which is corroborating (not sole) evidence.
questions.evidence: influora-ai/app/costs/pricing.py:34-58 (ModelRate incl. cache fields), :103-115 (PRICING_TABLE keyed by literal ids: claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929, claude-haiku-4-5-20251001, claude-opus-4-1-20250805, claude-3-5-haiku-20241022, gemini-2.5-flash), :191-241 (_resolve_rate, F-04 fallback-to-most-expensive-rate logic), :244-298 (estimate_cost_usd reading cache_read_input_tokens / cache_creation_input_tokens).
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Code-reading only — did not execute influora-ai/tests/costs/test_pricing.py or test_f01_f07_money_path.py to confirm the fix is actually covered/green (test files exist at influora-ai/tests/costs/ but were not run in this audit).

questions.question: Is there a per-workspace (per-brand) hard cap that stops one brand from consuming the entire global daily AI budget?
questions.why_it_matters: Without one, a single high-volume or misbehaving brand workspace can starve every other brand's Meera access for the rest of the day by burning the whole $15 global ceiling alone.
questions.answer: No. The only per-workspace check that BLOCKS is ai_workspace_daily_hard_cap_usd, read from WORKSPACE_DAILY_HARD_CAP_USD, which defaults to None/unset and is opt-in per gate.py's own docstring. Grepping all three production deploy compose files (hostinger, utho, utho-shared) and generate-env.sh finds AI_DAILY_SPEND_CEILING_USD, AI_SPEND_KILL_SWITCH and AI_CREATOR_MONTHLY_CAP_USD set, but WORKSPACE_DAILY_HARD_CAP_USD is set nowhere. The only workspace-level control actually active is ai_workspace_daily_soft_cap_usd ($3/day default), which chat.py logs as a WARNING only — it never blocks a call.
questions.evidence: influora-ai/app/costs/gate.py:10-21 (module docstring: hard cap is 'opt-in'), :81/:90-91 (hard_cap = settings.ai_workspace_daily_hard_cap_usd; only checked when both workspace_id AND hard_cap set); influora-ai/app/config.py:433-445 (ai_workspace_daily_soft_cap_usd is 'WARNING-only, not blocking'; ai_workspace_daily_hard_cap_usd via _get_optional_float, default None); grep across deploy/hostinger/docker-compose.hostinger.yml, deploy/utho/docker-compose.utho.yml, deploy/utho/docker-compose.utho-shared.yml, deploy/utho/generate-env.sh found zero occurrences of WORKSPACE_DAILY_HARD_CAP_USD.
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Cannot rule out an env var set out-of-repo directly on the host (e.g. via Hostinger/Utho panel or a .env file not checked into the RC) — config search was limited to committed deploy artifacts.

questions.question: How many paid provider calls does a single Meera voice conversation turn cost, end to end?
questions.why_it_matters: Voice is the most expensive interaction surface (3 chained providers per turn); undercounting this in a per-workflow cost model would misprice the whole creator-facing product.
questions.answer: A full voice round-trip is up to 3 separate billed external legs across 2 route handlers: (1) POST /voice/transcribe — Sarvam STT (flat $0.006/call, no token signal) THEN a Gemini 2.5 Flash 'cleanup_transcript' call (max_output_tokens=512); (2) POST /chat — 1 to tool_loop_max_iterations(=6) Claude calls (claude-sonnet-4-5, max_tokens 1536, 2048 on retry) to actually answer; (3) POST /voice/speak — Sarvam TTS, char-scaled at ~$0.3614/10,000 chars, capped by TTS_MAX_CHARS=500 in voice.py (≤$0.0181/call). Both voice legs independently call check_spend_gate AND check_creator_spend_gate before their respective provider call.
questions.evidence: influora-ai/app/routes/voice.py:73 (TTS_MAX_CHARS = 500), :385-460 (voice_transcribe: Sarvam STT then Gemini cleanup, both gated), :546-645 (voice_speak: Sarvam TTS char-scaled cost via estimate_sarvam_tts_cost_usd(result.billed_chars)); influora-ai/app/providers/gemini.py:286,303 (cleanup_transcript max_output_tokens=512); influora-ai/app/tools/loop.py:44 (DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS = 6); influora-ai/app/config.py:331-343 (meera_chat_max_tokens=1536, retry=2048).
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Static call-graph reconstruction, not a traced runtime request; the actual number of Claude tool-loop iterations for a typical (not worst-case) voice turn is not measurable from code alone — labeled ASSUMPTION in the cost table.

questions.question: Does the codebase account for the real Razorpay/RazorpayX transaction fee anywhere in the fee/ledger math, given the CEO ruling that 'platform absorbs Razorpay processing costs'?
questions.why_it_matters: If the 10%/15% platform take rate was sized assuming Razorpay's ~2% (payments) / per-payout fee is absorbed 'inside' that margin, but no code ever nets that cost out of platform revenue, Finance has no visibility into the real margin — it is an unmodeled, unaccounted-for COGS line.
questions.answer: The V42 migration adds a razorpay_absorbed_by_platform BOOLEAN (default TRUE) to platform_fee_config, explicitly documented as the CEO's 'Option A = platform absorbs Razorpay processing costs' decision. Searching the entire influora-api source for razorpayAbsorbedByPlatform shows it is only ever READ for admin display/audit-log purposes (PlatformFeeAdminService, AdminAuditLogService, PlatformFeeConfigDtos) — it is never consumed by BrandCampaignFeeService, PlatformFeeService, EscrowService or any ledger-posting code to actually net a Razorpay cost out of the platform revenue wallet. No RazorpayClient/RazorpayXClient response field for the actual per-transaction fee charged by Razorpay is captured or posted to any ledger/wallet at all.
questions.evidence: influora-api/src/main/resources/db/migration/V42__platform_fee_config_brand_fee_razorpay.sql:1-3,25 (razorpay_absorbed_by_platform column + CEO ruling comment); grep of razorpayAbsorbedByPlatform across influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora hits only domain/entity/PlatformFeeConfig.java, service/admin/AdminAuditLogService.java, service/admin/PlatformFeeAdminService.java, web/dto/admin/PlatformFeeConfigDtos.java — no service/*.java ledger/fee-calculation class references it; service/PlatformFeeService.java and service/BrandCampaignFeeService.java compute fees purely as a bps percentage of gross/budget with no Razorpay-fee subtraction term.
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Did not open every ledger-adjacent class in the repo (e.g. WalletLedgerService in full) to rule out a Razorpay-fee posting living somewhere unexpected; absence-of-evidence from a targeted grep, not an exhaustive negative proof.

questions.question: Does a brand's internal escrow refund also recover the original Razorpay gateway fee paid on top-up, or is that fee a sunk cost to the platform on every refund?
questions.why_it_matters: Refund cost is explicitly in scope; if escrow funding and escrow refund are pure internal wallet-ledger movements while the ORIGINAL top-up already paid Razorpay a real fee, every refunded campaign has a real, currently un-ledgered loss.
questions.answer: Escrow fund/refund (EscrowService.refund/refundInternal, LedgerEscrowBackend) are wallet-to-wallet ledger movements with no re-invocation of RazorpayClient — confirmed no razorpay import/call in the refund path. The wallet's INR balance was originally created via WalletTopUpService.topUp(), which does call RazorpayClient.createOrder() (a real, fee-bearing Razorpay payment). Since (per the prior question) no code anywhere nets a Razorpay fee against the ledger, a refunded escrow returns the brand's full gross INR to their wallet while the platform has already paid Razorpay's real transaction fee on the original top-up with no recovery mechanism — consistent with the broader 'unmodeled Razorpay cost' finding, not a separately-coded defect.
questions.evidence: influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/EscrowService.java:946-998 (refund/refundInternal call escrowBackend.refund, an internal LedgerEscrowBackend posting, not RazorpayClient); influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/WalletTopUpService.java:70,161 (RazorpayClient.createOrder is the only Razorpay touchpoint for money entering a wallet).
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Did not open LedgerEscrowBackend.java in full to rule out a fee-clawback line item; inferred from call-site absence, not from reading that whole class.

questions.question: What is the actual GST treatment on the platform's own fee income (brand 10% / creator 15%), and is it computed correctly?
questions.why_it_matters: Incorrect CGST/SGST vs IGST classification on commission invoices is a real compliance and cash exposure, separate from AI/API costs but squarely a CFO concern.
questions.answer: GstSplitUtil.compute() implements the standard India GST rule (same first-2-digit GSTIN state code → CGST+SGST split 50/50 with rounding residual absorbed into SGST; different/unknown state → full IGST) and is shared by every D14 PDF invoice renderer including CommissionInvoiceService for both the brand-fee and creator-fee legs. This is a reasonable, standard implementation on its face.
questions.evidence: influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/GstSplitUtil.java:1-46 (compute() method, intra-state vs inter-state logic, rounding-residual handling).
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Did not verify the GST RATE (18%?) is applied correctly upstream of this split, nor trace a real invoice's numbers end-to-end against CommissionInvoiceService/CommissionInvoicePdfService — this only confirms the CGST/SGST/IGST split math itself, not the full tax pipeline.

questions.question: Is a single AI-bound worker process (rather than multiple, unsynchronized workers) enforced, so the Redis-backed daily ceiling can't be silently bypassed by scaling?
questions.why_it_matters: The whole spend-tracking design (F-05 reservations, Redis-shared counters) explicitly assumes one process; if ops ever scales influora-ai horizontally without also fixing this, the daily ceiling reverts to a per-process ceiling.
questions.answer: Yes, and it fails closed. The Dockerfile pins uvicorn to --workers 1, and a comment states 'influora-ai refuses to boot with more than one uvicorn worker' — i.e., there is an explicit boot-time guard (app/costs/worker_guard.py, 98 lines) rather than a mere convention. This is a genuine safety control but also means influora-ai cannot horizontally scale for THROUGHPUT (only for isolated environments/replicas each running their own single worker, each with their own $15/day ceiling unless they share the same Redis — in which case they'd correctly share the ceiling but also share a single bottlenecked process per container).
questions.evidence: influora-ai/Dockerfile:49-54 (CMD pins --workers 1, comment: 'app.main refuses to boot with --workers > 1'); influora-ai/app/costs/worker_guard.py exists (98 lines, not fully read in this pass) as the presumed enforcement point; deploy/hostinger/docker-compose.hostinger.yml:425 repeats the same comment.
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Did not open worker_guard.py's full source to confirm the exact mechanism (env var check vs multiprocessing detection) or test that boot actually fails with --workers 2.

questions.question: Are there any AI-adjacent endpoints in this RC with NO spend-gate call at all — a free-credit-abuse or cost-explosion path that bypasses the ceiling entirely?
questions.why_it_matters: A single ungated route calling Claude/Gemini/Sarvam would be a direct path to unbounded billing regardless of how well the gated routes are designed.
questions.answer: Every route file that imports a provider client also imports and calls app.costs.gate.check_spend_gate before the call: chat.py, voice.py (both transcribe and speak), analyze_site.py, brand_safety.py, creator_suggestion.py, trend_tag.py. No AI route was found that skips the gate. The one non-gated, unbounded-frequency trigger identified is Java-side, not Python-side: OnboardingService.saveBrandCompany triggers AnalyzeSiteTriggerService.trigger() every time a brand saves/changes its website URL, with no cooldown/rate-limit found in AnalyzeSiteTriggerService.java — but every resulting call still passes through analyze_site.py's own check_spend_gate on the Python side, so the exposure is bounded by the global ceiling, just not individually rate-limited per brand.
questions.evidence: grep of 'check_spend_gate' across influora-ai/app/routes/*.py shows it present and called in chat.py:491, voice.py:445 and :597, analyze_site.py:160, brand_safety.py:287, creator_suggestion.py:264, trend_tag.py:223; influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/brand/AnalyzeSiteTriggerService.java:38-40 ('Call site: OnboardingService.saveBrandCompany calls trigger whenever a brand saves/changes their website URL') with no cooldown/rateLimit/throttle token found in that file via targeted grep.
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Did not verify by grep whether OnboardingService.saveBrandCompany itself has a higher-level rate limit (e.g. a generic per-endpoint API rate limiter) that would blunt this; only AnalyzeSiteTriggerService.java itself was checked for a cooldown.

questions.question: Is the per-creator monthly AI cost cap ($0.75/month default) actually enforced BEFORE a provider call, or only logged after the fact?
questions.why_it_matters: A creator-facing free product surface (Meera for Creators) is the highest fan-out, lowest-revenue-per-user AI cost center in the system — if this cap is soft/advisory, per-creator AI cost could exceed the ~500-750 INR commission it's sized against.
questions.answer: Blocking, per the code's own design intent and call-site ordering. config.py's comment states it is 'Enforced BLOCKING by app.costs.spend_tracker.check_creator_spend_gate before any provider call' and voice.py's _creator_voice_gate() is called and checked (cap_blocked short-circuits to a friendly fallback message) before check_spend_gate() and before either Sarvam/Gemini call in voice_transcribe.
questions.evidence: influora-ai/app/config.py:447-457 (ai_creator_monthly_cap_usd doc, 'Enforced BLOCKING ... before any provider call'); influora-ai/app/routes/voice.py:427-434 (_creator_voice_gate called and cap_blocked returns early, BEFORE the check_spend_gate call at line 445).
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Did not open app/costs/spend_tracker.py's check_creator_spend_gate implementation itself (1106-line file, only referenced, not read in full) to confirm the monthly counter reset-at-UTC-month-boundary logic is correct and race-free the way the daily F-05 fix is.

findings.title: No per-workspace BLOCKING hard cap is configured in any production deploy artifact; a single brand can exhaust the entire global $15/day AI ceiling alone
findings.evidence: app/costs/gate.py:81,90-91 only enforces ai_workspace_daily_hard_cap_usd (env WORKSPACE_DAILY_HARD_CAP_USD) when that var is set; it is unset in deploy/hostinger/docker-compose.hostinger.yml, deploy/utho/docker-compose.utho.yml, deploy/utho/docker-compose.utho-shared.yml and deploy/utho/generate-env.sh (all three grepped, zero hits). The only active per-workspace control, ai_workspace_daily_soft_cap_usd ($3/day), is documented in app/config.py:433-436 as 'WARNING-only, not blocking'.
findings.impact: One noisy or abusive brand workspace can consume the full $15/day global ceiling before its own 8pm meeting is over, tripping AI_SPEND_CEILING_REACHED for every OTHER brand's Meera chat/voice/analyze-site/brand-safety calls for the rest of the UTC day. This is a fairness/availability cost-explosion vector, not a runaway-total-spend vector (the global ceiling still holds spend to $15/day) — but it converts a well-designed global backstop into a single-tenant-can-DoS-everyone-else situation.
findings.recommended_fix: Set WORKSPACE_DAILY_HARD_CAP_USD in all three production compose files (e.g. $3-5/workspace/day, matching or slightly above the existing $3 soft-cap value already chosen), and confirm chat.py already passes workspace_id to check_spend_gate (it does, per gate.py's own docstring at line 53) so the hard cap activates automatically once the env var is set.
findings.verification_required: After setting the env var in a staging deploy, drive one workspace's chat volume past the hard cap and confirm AI_WORKSPACE_SPEND_CAP_REACHED is returned while a second workspace's calls still succeed (E4 runtime proof).

findings.title: Real Razorpay/RazorpayX transaction fees are never modeled, tracked, or netted against platform revenue anywhere in the codebase, despite an explicit CEO ruling that the platform absorbs them
findings.evidence: V42__platform_fee_config_brand_fee_razorpay.sql:1-3,25 documents the CEO ruling 'Option A = platform absorbs Razorpay processing costs' via a razorpay_absorbed_by_platform BOOLEAN; grepping razorpayAbsorbedByPlatform across the whole influora-api source shows it is read only by admin display/audit-log code (PlatformFeeAdminService.java, AdminAuditLogService.java, PlatformFeeConfigDtos.java) and never by PlatformFeeService.java, BrandCampaignFeeService.java, or any WalletLedgerService posting path. No RazorpayClient/RazorpayXClient response is captured into any ledger line representing the actual gateway fee charged.
findings.location: influora-api/src/main/resources/db/migration/V42__platform_fee_config_brand_fee_razorpay.sql:23-27; influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/PlatformFeeService.java (fee = bps only); influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/BrandCampaignFeeService.java (fee = bps only); influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/integration/razorpay/RazorpayXClient.java, RazorpayClient.java (no fee-field capture found)
findings.impact: The 10% brand / 15% creator take rate is presented internally as the platform's margin, but the real Razorpay payment-gateway fee (~2% on card/UPI payments) and RazorpayX payout fee (per-transaction, varies by mode: IMPS/NEFT) are silently subtracted from that margin with zero ledger visibility. Finance cannot see the true net margin per campaign from the ledger alone, and at volume this is real, un-forecast COGS that could materially erode the stated 10%/15% economics, especially on high-frequency small-ticket payouts where a flat per-transaction RazorpayX fee is a larger percentage of the transfer.
findings.recommended_fix: Capture RazorpayXClient's actual per-payout fee (available in its API response) and RazorpayClient's per-order fee, and post them as a distinct ledger line (e.g. a new WalletTransactionType.GATEWAY_FEE) against the platform revenue wallet so PlatformFeeAdminService/AdminRevenueService can report a true net-of-gateway-cost margin, not just gross bps revenue.
findings.verification_required: Confirm with Razorpay's dashboard/settlement reports what the actual historical gateway fee percentage has been on live volume (referenced in memory: project_meta_razorpay_live_0913.md notes a real Rs 1,000 wallet credit was proven live 2026-09-13), then reconcile against zero ledger entries for that fee in the DB.

findings.title: influora-ai is architecturally capped at one worker process per container (boot refuses --workers > 1), which is a correctness requirement for the cost-ceiling design but also a hard throughput/cost-scaling ceiling
findings.evidence: influora-ai/Dockerfile:49-54 pins `--workers 1` with a comment that app.main refuses to boot with more workers; deploy/hostinger/docker-compose.hostinger.yml:425 repeats the same note tying it to the Redis-backed spend-tracker design.
findings.location: influora-ai/Dockerfile:49-54; influora-ai/app/costs/worker_guard.py (98 lines, presumed enforcement, not fully read)
findings.impact: This is the CORRECT tradeoff given the current spend-tracker design (multi-worker would silently multiply the effective daily ceiling without the Redis coordination this comment implies is still incomplete for >1 worker), but it means each influora-ai container instance can only serve as many concurrent Claude/Gemini/Sarvam calls as one Python asyncio process supports. At real user-growth scale this becomes a latency/availability cost tradeoff: either accept single-process throughput limits per replica, or someone eventually removes the guard without first verifying the Redis-backed tracker (spend_tracker.py, 1106 lines, not fully audited this pass) is safe under true multi-process concurrency — which would reopen exactly the F-05 race this guard exists to prevent.
findings.recommended_fix: Document this constraint explicitly in a scaling runbook (scale by adding container REPLICAS, each still --workers 1, all pointed at the same REDIS_URL, never by raising --workers) so a future operator does not "fix" a perceived throughput problem by removing the boot guard.
findings.verification_required: Read influora-ai/app/costs/worker_guard.py and app/costs/spend_tracker.py in full to confirm the Redis-backed counter is safe under concurrent REPLICAS (as opposed to concurrent workers within one process) — not verified in this pass.

findings.title: No cooldown/rate-limit found on AnalyzeSiteTriggerService's per-brand-URL-save trigger of the Gemini-backed /analyze-site call
findings.evidence: influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/brand/AnalyzeSiteTriggerService.java:38-40 documents the call site as 'OnboardingService.saveBrandCompany calls trigger whenever a brand saves/changes their website URL'; targeted grep for cooldown/rateLimit/lastAnalyzedAt/throttle in that file returned no matches.
findings.location: influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/brand/AnalyzeSiteTriggerService.java (full file, cooldown search); influora-ai/app/routes/analyze_site.py:160 (per-call spend gate still applies)
findings.impact: Each call costs one Gemini 2.5 Flash call at up to 4096 output tokens (~$0.001-0.003 at gemini-2.5-flash's $0.30/$2.50-per-MTok rate) — individually cheap, but a brand repeatedly editing/re-saving its website URL (deliberately or via a buggy frontend retry loop) can re-trigger this an unbounded number of times per day with no per-brand cooldown, bounded only by the shared global $15/day ceiling (which every OTHER AI feature also draws from).
findings.recommended_fix: Add a per-workspace cooldown (e.g. 1 analyze-site trigger per URL-change per N minutes/hours) in AnalyzeSiteTriggerService.trigger(), independent of the global spend ceiling, so this one feature cannot crowd out chat/voice/brand-safety spend for the rest of the org.
findings.verification_required: Confirm whether OnboardingService.saveBrandCompany has a higher-level generic rate limiter (not checked in this pass) that would already blunt this before it reaches AnalyzeSiteTriggerService.

findings.title: Minor doc/code drift: pricing.py's TTS cost comment cites TTS_MAX_CHARS=200 but voice.py's actual constant is 500
findings.evidence: influora-ai/app/costs/pricing.py:138-140 comment: 'the flat $0.006 under-bills a max-length (TTS_MAX_CHARS=200, see routes/voice.py) call by ~20%'; influora-ai/app/routes/voice.py:73: `TTS_MAX_CHARS = 500`.
findings.impact: No financial impact — estimate_sarvam_tts_cost_usd() is char-scaled off the ACTUAL text length sent (result.billed_chars), not off this stale comment's constant, so billing itself is correct. This is purely a stale-comment drift risk: a future reader trusting the comment's '200 chars / Rs 0.60' worked example while the real cap is 500 chars (up to Rs 1.50 at the real rate) would under-estimate the true per-call TTS ceiling by 2.5x when reasoning about worst-case cost from the comment alone.
findings.recommended_fix: Update the pricing.py comment to reference the live TTS_MAX_CHARS=500 constant (or better, import and interpolate it rather than hardcoding the number in a comment, so this drift cannot recur).
findings.verification_required: None further needed — both files were opened and the discrepancy is directly confirmed.

findings.title: No aggregate per-workspace storage quota on Cloudflare R2 uploads (only a per-file 500MB video cap)
findings.evidence: influora-api/src/main/resources/application.yml:374-381 configures R2_MAX_VIDEO_BYTES (524288000 = 500MB) as the only size-related setting; targeted grep of UploadService.java and R2StorageService.java for QUOTA/storage limit/StorageQuota returned no matches.
findings.impact: R2's own pricing (no egress fee, ~$0.015/GB-month storage) makes this a low-severity vector — unbounded uploads per workspace scale storage cost roughly linearly and slowly, unlike the AI cost surface. Flagged for completeness per the audit's cost-explosion-vector requirement, not as a go-live blocker.
findings.recommended_fix: If not already tracked at the infra billing level, add a soft per-workspace total-storage-used counter (queryable, not necessarily blocking) so Finance has visibility before this becomes material at scale.
findings.verification_required: Confirm with Cloudflare's actual R2 bill whether storage cost has been material to date; this finding is speculative/low-confidence and was not chased further given the higher-priority AI/payment cost surfaces.

Code-level and config-level evidence is strong (E3), but no runtime trip of the ceiling was observed (would require E4 load test in a safe env, out of scope).

area.name: AI provider cost governance and payment economics
area.status: Mostly sound design with real prior-incident fixes documented in code, but production config has a fairness gap (no per-workspace hard cap) and a real accounting gap (Razorpay fees never netted against revenue).
area.main_evidence: Consistent, code-verified spend-gate call ordering across all 6 AI routes; Redis-shared, single-worker-enforced spend tracker; explicit, dollar-quantified prior-incident fix comments (F-01 cache billing, F-04 model-price fallback, F-05 reservation race) that read as genuine post-mortems rather than aspirational claims; DB-migration-documented CEO-approved fee/GST/Razorpay-absorption ruling.
area.main_uncertainty: No runtime/load-test evidence that the $15/day ceiling or the per-creator monthly cap actually trips correctly under concurrency in this RC specifically (E4); did not read app/costs/spend_tracker.py (1106 lines) or worker_guard.py in full, so the Redis-coordination correctness claims rest on code comments plus call-site ordering, not a full trace of the tracker's own internals.
area.limitations: Static, read-only, single-pass audit against a clean checkout of one commit; no tests were executed; no live/staging environment was probed; Razorpay's actual live fee schedule and settlement reports were not available to this audit to quantify ROH-02's dollar impact precisely.

extra:
COST-PER-WORKFLOW TABLE (all figures ASSUMPTION-labeled where they extrapolate beyond a single directly-cited constant; Anthropic/Gemini/Sarvam list prices are as hardcoded in influora-ai/app/costs/pricing.py, verified 2026-07-11/12 per that file's own docstring — re-verify against current Anthropic/Google/Sarvam price pages before using for real budgeting, since AI list prices change):

1) TEXT CHAT TURN (brand or creator, via POST /chat, Claude only)
   - Model: claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 ($3/MTok in, $15/MTok out, per pricing.py:105)
   - Calls per turn: 1 (simple Q&A) to up to 6 (tool_loop_max_iterations, loop.py:44) for a multi-step flow like a Meera-guided campaign create
   - max_tokens: 1536 normal / 2048 on the one server-side retry (config.py:331-343)
   - Prompt caching: Block A (persona+tools, cached) + Block B (per-brand profile, cached) per prompt/assembler.py's cache_control:ephemeral markers — code comment in providers/claude.py:4 claims caching is 'the ~65% cost lever' but this percentage is a design-doc claim, ASSUMPTION, not independently re-derived in this audit
   - ASSUMPTION cost per simple 1-call turn (200 tokens fresh input on a cache HIT + 400 output tokens, no cache write): ~$0.0064 (200*$0.000003 + 400*$0.000015, ignoring the cached-block tokens which are billed at 0.1x input rate per pricing.py:57-58)
   - ASSUMPTION cost for a worst-case 6-iteration tool-heavy turn at similar per-call size: ~6x the above, roughly $0.02-0.04

2) VOICE CHAT TURN (creator or brand, POST /voice/transcribe + /chat + /voice/speak)
   - Leg 1 (STT): Sarvam flat $0.006/call regardless of length (pricing.py:133,153-163)
   - Leg 1b (Gemini cleanup): gemini-2.5-flash ($0.30/MTok in, $2.50/MTok out), max_output_tokens=512 (gemini.py:303) — ASSUMPTION ~$0.0006/call at typical usage
   - Leg 2 (Claude reply): same as text chat turn above, 1-6 calls
   - Leg 3 (TTS): Sarvam, char-scaled at $0.3614/10,000 chars (pricing.py:146-150), capped at TTS_MAX_CHARS=500 in voice.py:73 => max $0.0181/call, ASSUMPTION typical ~$0.005-0.010/call for a short spoken reply
   - ASSUMPTION total per voice turn (typical, 1 Claude call): ~$0.006 (STT) + $0.0006 (Gemini) + $0.0064 (Claude) + $0.008 (TTS) \u2approx $0.021/turn
   - Both /voice/transcribe and /voice/speak independently pass the per-creator MONTHLY cap check before spending anything (config.py:447-457)

3) TREND-SPARK NUDGE (1 cheap Claude Haiku phrasing call)
   - Model: claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 ($1/MTok in, $5/MTok out, pricing.py:106), TRENDSPARK_MAX_TOKENS=300 (config.py:365-367)
   - ASSUMPTION cost per call (~150 input, 150 output tokens): ~$0.00098

4) CREATOR CO-PILOT SUGGESTION (POST /internal/creator-suggestion, 1 Claude call)
   - Model: defaults to TRENDSPARK_MODEL (Haiku), CREATOR_COPILOT_MAX_TOKENS=300 (config.py:383-385)
   - ASSUMPTION cost similar to Trend-Spark nudge above, ~$0.001/call. Client NEVER throws — always falls back to a free templated reply on any failure (CreatorSuggestionAiClient.java javadoc), so cost exposure is capped at exactly this one call per suggestion request, never retried by this client itself.

5) BRAND-SAFETY GARM CLASSIFICATION (POST /internal/brand-safety, batched)
   - Model: defaults to CLAUDE_MODEL (Sonnet), BRAND_SAFETY_MAX_TOKENS=4096 (config.py:421-423), batched up to BRAND_SAFETY_MAX_ITEMS_PER_CALL=25 items/call (config.py:412-414)
   - ASSUMPTION cost per 25-item batch call (~2000 input tokens of captions/metadata + up to 4096 output tokens worst case): could be as high as ~$0.067/call at the FULL 4096-token output ceiling, though real classification output is typically far shorter than the ceiling

6) ANALYZE-SITE (POST /analyze-site, Gemini only, triggered on brand URL save)
   - Model: gemini-2.5-flash, max_output_tokens=4096 (gemini.py:259, a THINKING model where reasoning tokens count against this ceiling per that line's own comment)
   - ASSUMPTION cost per call (~5000 input tokens of scraped page text + up to 4096 output/thinking tokens worst case): roughly $0.0025-0.012/call
   - No per-brand cooldown found (ROH-04) — re-triggerable on every URL save

PAYMENT ECONOMICS (Razorpay/RazorpayX, V41/V42 migrations, CEO-approved 2026 ruling):
   - Brand-side platform fee: 10.00% (1000 bps) of campaign budget at publish, charged as 'fee on top' — does NOT touch budgetMin/budgetMax or creator payout base (BrandCampaignFeeService.java javadoc). Pro-plan brands get 7.00% (700 bps) instead, resolved per-workspace, fail-open to the 10% global rate on any plan-lookup error (never fails open to a LOWER rate).
   - Creator-side platform fee: 15.00% (1500 bps, default_fee_bps in V41/V42) deducted at escrow release.
   - Razorpay/RazorpayX processing costs: 'absorbed by platform' per CEO ruling (razorpay_absorbed_by_platform=TRUE), but this is UNMODELED in code — see ROH-02. No ledger line nets an actual gateway fee against platform revenue anywhere found.
   - GST: CGST+SGST (intra-state) vs IGST (inter-state) computed via GstSplitUtil.compute() based on GSTIN state-code comparison, shared across commission and subscription invoicing.
   - Refunds: escrow refund is a pure internal wallet-ledger reversal (EscrowService.refundInternal -> LedgerEscrowBackend), it does NOT re-touch Razorpay — meaning the ORIGINAL top-up's Razorpay gateway fee (paid via WalletTopUpService -> RazorpayClient.createOrder) is a sunk, un-recovered, and un-ledgered cost on every refunded campaign (see ROH-02/refund question above).

COST-EXPLOSION VECTORS AT SCALE (ranked):
   1. [ROH-01, P2] No per-workspace BLOCKING hard cap active in production — one workspace can consume 100% of the shared $15/day global ceiling, denial-of-service-by-cost-starvation against every other tenant, not a runaway-total-spend risk per se.
   2. [ROH-02, P2] Real Razorpay/RazorpayX fees are entirely unmodeled against platform revenue — at volume, an unaccounted, unbudgeted COGS line that could silently erode the stated 10%/15% margin, worse on high-frequency low-ticket creator payouts where a flat per-transaction gateway fee is a larger fraction of the transfer.
   3. [ROH-04, P3] No per-brand cooldown on the URL-save-triggered analyze-site Gemini call — cheap per call but individually un-rate-limited, bounded only by the shared global ceiling.
   4. [ROH-03, P3] Single-worker-per-container architecture is a deliberate, currently-correct safety tradeoff, but is also a hard throughput ceiling that risk being 'fixed' incorrectly by a future operator without re-verifying the Redis-backed tracker's multi-process safety.
   5. [ROH-06, P3] No aggregate per-workspace R2 storage quota — low severity given R2's pricing model, flagged for completeness only.

NO REVENUE OR VOLUME FIGURES WERE INVENTED for this report; all dollar estimates above are per-call/per-token extrapolations from pricing.py's own list-price constants and are explicitly labeled ASSUMPTION where they go beyond a single directly-cited code constant.
